confirmed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation; users can repeatedly activate arrows while results load.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and the cure is trivially available and unused. `PaginationBar.vue:10,24` bind `:disabled` ONLY to `!hasPrev`/`!hasNext` — there is no busy/pending input at all; the component's prop surface (`:37-42`) has no `loading`. The producer ships the exact affordance: `Button.vue.d.ts:16` `loading?: boolean` — "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles" — implemented at `button-Bu9F4uU6.js:35` (`m = loading || disabled`) with an activation-suppressing handler at `:44`. The in-flight flag is already published by both ports (`demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:39,96` and `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:52,138` expose `loading`) and is already consumed for skeletons by the panels (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16), but is never threaded to PaginationBar. Double-activation is executably reproduced in-repo at `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:51-62` ("C2: double-click Next skips a page and leaves two flights in the air" — asserts page lands on 3 and offsets [20,40] are both requested).

confirmed.claim: Events carry no destination/request identity, so parent and child can race; out-of-order responses are possible.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED as to the RACE, but the axis misattributes the cause and therefore prescribes the wrong cure. `PaginationBar.vue:44-47` emits bare `prev`/`next`; handlers are `audit.prevPage`/`nextPage` (AdminAuditPanel.vue:88-89) and `flagged.prevPage`/`nextPage` (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:131-132). The real defect is in the composables: `useAdminAudit.ts:48-71` and `useAdminFlagged.ts:59-79` carry NO request-sequence token and NO in-flight bail — every `loadX()` unconditionally assigns `entries/items = res.data` and `total = res.total` on resolve, so two overlapping flights resolve last-wins regardless of which page they were for. Also `loading` is a plain boolean, so the `finally` of the FIRST flight (useAdminAudit.ts:68-70) clears `loading` while the second is still airborne, retracting the skeleton early. Executably reproduced in-repo at `docs/.../AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:27-49` ("C1: out-of-order responses — the STALE page wins (no request sequencing)", asserting `page===2` while `items[0].paletteSlug==="page1-row"`). CURE CORRECTION: putting a destination in the emit (the axis's prescription) does not fix this — the child would still be a dumb relay and the stale write would still land. The structurally sound fix is a monotonic request-generation token in the composable, discarding responses whose generation is superseded.

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; page values outside [1,pageCount] are rendered verbatim.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED ONLY for the `page > pageCount` limb; the other limbs are unreachable (see killed C-1-limbs). `PaginationBar.vue:3` guards solely on `pageCount > 1` and `:18` interpolates `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}` with no clamp. `page > pageCount` IS reachable in the live tree via the un-clamped local decrement in `useAdminFlagged.ts:87` / `:99` (`total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` with no page clamp and no reload). Worked example: pageSize 20 (`useAdminFlagged.ts:51`), total 41, page 3 → pageCount = Math.max(1, ceil(41/20)) = 3 (`:55`); dismiss one row → total 40 → pageCount 2 while page stays 3 → the bar renders (2 > 1) and literally reads "Page 3 of 2". Here `hasNext=false`, `hasPrev=true` (`:56-57`) so the user can still escape via Previous — which is why this variant is MAJOR and not the BLOCKER; the unrecoverable sibling case is filed separately under MISSED.

confirmed.claim: aria-live announces page-text mutations that are not bound to completion of the corresponding list request.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED structurally. `PaginationBar.vue:17` marks the counter `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`, and `:18` renders `page` directly. `useAdminAudit.ts:73-78` (`nextPage`) increments `page.value++` SYNCHRONOUSLY and only then calls the async `loadAuditLog()`; identical shape at `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110`. Vue flushes the reactive text update on the next microtask tick, long before the network promise resolves, so the region announces "Page 3 of 5" while the panel is still showing the previous page's rows (or, once `loading` flips, skeletons at AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38). The announcement is therefore bound to intent, not to commit. Severity held to MINOR: announcing navigation intent is a defensible pattern and no false content is spoken — the counter is accurate about the requested page. Whether a real screen reader's queueing makes this audible as a mis-ordering is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE (no AT available under probe parsimony). Motion/PRM law is not implicated: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:274` lists PaginationBar C·D·L under "§7.4 No motion content — vacuously cleared", so no M-xx row constrains any verdict here.

killed.claim: `hasNext`/`hasPrev` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled; the four scalars can contradict each other.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the contradiction is unreachable in the live tree, and the axis reached this verdict only because it declared itself "Source-only" (challenge-C-implementation.md:3, challenge-L-library.md:3) and never opened the two files that produce the props. There are exactly two call sites, and BOTH derive all four scalars from the same two numbers. `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:44-46`: `pageCount = computed(() => Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize)))`, `hasNext = computed(() => page.value < pageCount.value)`, `hasPrev = computed(() => page.value > 1)`. These are `computed` refs, not free-floating booleans, so "Page 1 of 2 with Previous enabled" would require `1 > 1` to evaluate true. The bindings are direct (AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130) with no transformation. The "four unrelated scalars" framing further presumes a library boundary that does not exist: PaginationBar is a PRIVATE component — `grep -rn PaginationBar demo/ --include=*.ts` returns zero hits, and the admin barrel `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:3-7` exports only the five panels, deliberately ("NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)"). killed.claim: `page=0`, negative values, or non-integer values are rendered verbatim.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — these three limbs are unreachable. `page` is initialised to `1` (`useAdminAudit.ts:37`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:50`) and the ONLY mutations are `page.value++` behind `if (hasNext.value)` and `page.value--` behind `if (hasPrev.value)` (`useAdminAudit.ts:73-85`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117`), plus a reset to the literal `1` at AdminAuditPanel.vue:114. Since `hasPrev = page > 1` gates every decrement, `page` can never reach 0 or go negative; since every mutation is ±1 from the integer 1, it can never be non-integer. Likewise `pageCount` can never be zero or negative: `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(...))` (`useAdminAudit.ts:44`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:55`) pins it to ≥1 and `Math.ceil` pins it to an integer. Only the `page > pageCount` limb is live (confirmed separately).

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals.
killed.refutation: REFUTED AS STATED (though it gestures near the real defect). (a) The "invalid negative/zero totals" limb is impossible: `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (useAdminFlagged.ts:55, useAdminAudit.ts:44) cannot yield ≤0. (b) The loading and error limbs are already discharged by the PANELS, which own dedicated branches: skeletons at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18 / AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38 and a distinct error EmptyState at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33 / AdminAuditPanel.vue:42-53, both carrying provenance comments ("W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger"). Hiding a pagination control when there is exactly one page is standard correct behaviour, not a conflation. (c) The "unknown count" limb is vacuous: `total` is initialised to 0 and only ever assigned from a resolved response, so pre-load state is covered by the loading branch. The genuine harm of the `pageCount > 1` guard is NOT ambiguity of meaning — it is that the guard removes the user's only escape control at the exact moment they need it, which this axis did not see; filed as the MISSED blocker.

The compiled component consumes it at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:52-53`, emitting `data-icon-only` and, notably, `data-control-target` (the hit-target hook) ONLY when set. PaginationBar sets neither, so both attributes are absent and the buttons fall to default non-square geometry. This is not a speculative API: the repo already uses the kebab template form correctly in comparable icon buttons — `demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:20` and `:32`, `demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:65`, `demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:166` and `:176` (21 `icon-only` occurrences across demo/). missed.claim: MINOR — the `aria-live` region is nested INSIDE the `v-if`, so it is created together with its first content and destroyed/recreated on every pageCount 1↔2 transition; a live region must pre-exist its mutations to announce reliably.
missed.proof: Missed by C-5 and D-4, which both reasoned only about announcement TIMING relative to the request, never about region LIFETIME. `PaginationBar.vue:2-3` opens the wrapper `<div v-if="pageCount > 1">` and the live region at `:17` (`aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`) sits inside it, closing at `:30`. Consequence: when a collection grows from one page to two, the region is inserted into the accessibility tree already populated with "Page 1 of 2" — assistive tech generally does not announce content present at region-creation time, only subsequent mutations — so the transition into a paginated state is silent. Symmetrically, when pageCount drops to 1 the region is torn out of the DOM, which is also the mechanism of the BLOCKER above. Ordinary page-to-page stepping (region already mounted, text mutates) does announce correctly, which is why this is MINOR rather than MAJOR. Whether a specific screen reader suppresses the mount-time content is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE under probe parsimony; the DOM lifetime itself is statically certain. Cure: hoist the live region outside the `v-if` (or swap `v-if` for `v-show` on the wrapper) so the region is stable for the panel's lifetime.

The same discipline is applied consistently across the admin cluster (AdminAuditPanel.vue:29-31, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:9-11, :97,:100).

Paired correctly with `aria-atomic="true"` so the counter is announced as one sentence rather than as two mutated numbers.

EXCELLENT (producer-side) — glass-ui 7.0.0's axis vocabulary is unusually disciplined API design, and it explicitly anticipates precisely the mistake this component makes. `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts:16` documents the tone axis as "the semantic status register (`--<tone>` token cohort); NEVER a `variant` member" — the producer names and forbids the collapsed-variant anti-pattern in the type declaration itself. `Button.vue.d.ts:8-18` follows through with orthogonal `emphasis` (visual priority, "It does not change the command's semantics") vs `tone` (semantic intent), each documented at the property.

The provenance comments state the invariant crisply — "W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger" — which is exactly the failure mode most list UIs ship. Note this makes the flag queue's SILENT dismiss/delete failures (useAdminFlagged.ts:88-90, :100-102, console.warn only) an inconsistency with the surrounding standard rather than an absence of one.

killed.claim: Events do not include the destination, so parent and child can race against changing props.

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals.

(a) 'invalid negative/zero totals': structurally impossible — `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize))` (useAdminAudit.ts:44, useAdminFlagged.ts:55) floors at 1 and can never be negative or zero. Only a thin sliver survives — on very first paint total=0 → pageCount=1 → the bar is absent — but that is 'not yet loaded', not the conflation D describes.

So the `aria-disabled` path is unreachable here and the real `disabled` attribute is always used, reinforced by `dist/components/button/styles.css`: `.button:disabled { pointer-events: none; }`. Symmetric on Previous reaching page 1. Note for the cure: because glass-ui hard-codes native `disabled` for `as="button"`, the component cannot opt into the focus-preserving `aria-disabled` idiom without a producer change — this is a glass-ui relay item, not a demo-local fix.

(:42-47) while PaginationBar simultaneously renders 'Page 3 of 7' with both arrows live; pressing Next runs useAdminAudit.ts:73-78, increments `page` to 4, announces 'Page 4 of 7' through the `aria-live` region (PaginationBar.vue:17), and fires another doomed request — advertising navigable pages of a corpus that cannot be fetched. On failure the same list renders below 'The ledger is unreachable.' — the panel contradicts itself. Identical at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue: chain ends :37, unguarded `v-for` at :44.

missed.claim: Unsequenced fetches let an out-of-order response overwrite a newer page — the real race that challenge-C-3 groped for and mis-located in the emit signature.
missed.proof: `useAdminAudit.ts:48-71` has no request token, no abort controller and no generation counter; it unconditionally commits with `entries.value = res.data` (:61) and `total.value = res.total` (:62) in whatever order responses arrive, and `loading.value = false` in a `finally` (:69) that the FIRST settling request clears. Reachable because nothing blocks double activation (see C-4): two fast Next presses advance `page` 1→2→3 (:75) and issue two overlapping `getAuditLog` calls with `offset` 20 and 40 (:55). If the offset-20 response lands second, `entries` ends up holding page 2's rows while the counter and `page` ref both read 3, `hasNext` is computed against that wrong page, and `loading` already read false after the first settle. Identical shape in useAdminFlagged.ts:59+. Correct cure is a generation guard in the composable, not a payload on the emit.

missed.claim: The `aria-live` region is nested INSIDE the `v-if` it depends on, so the announcements at the boundaries of the bar's own existence are lost.

A live region must be present in the accessibility tree BEFORE its contents change for assistive tech to reliably announce a mutation; a region inserted already populated is generally not announced. Failure: on first successful load `pageCount` goes 1→5, so the region and its text 'Page 1 of 5' enter the DOM together and the arrival of pagination is silent. Symmetrically, when a filter narrows results to one page (AdminAuditPanel.vue:111-117 sets `page = 1` and reloads → `pageCount` 1) the entire region is unmounted, so the disappearance of pagination is also silent while the visible layout changes. The fix is to keep the region mounted and empty it, rather than gating it. Exact announcement behaviour varies by AT/browser pairing — see unproven.

confirmed.claim: `contain: content` is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow. Its visual consequences are not part of the design contract.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and PROVEN CONCRETE — the axes gestured, I measured the mechanism. `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52` sets `.palette-card-grid { contain: content }`. Per CSS Containment, `content` == `layout paint style`; `paint` clips the whole subtree at the element's PADDING edge. The grid has NO padding (`class="palette-card-grid grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]"`, :4) so its padding edge == its content edge. Grid items in `grid-cols-1` stretch to full column width, so each PaletteCard's border-box left/right edges COINCIDE with the clip boundary. PaletteCard carries `cartoon-surface` (`demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:19`), defined in `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css:1` as `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }`, and `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-lead), -5px 5px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-mid), -7px 7px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-contact)` (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1`) — a LEFT+DOWN cast extending up to 7px left and 7px down, at 32-46% ink (`--cartoon-ink-lead: color-mix(in oklab, var(--cartoon-ink) 32-46%, transparent)`). The same geometry is carried a second time by the `.cartoon-cast` child span (`PaletteCard.vue:30`; rule at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css:1` — `position:absolute; inset:0; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md)`). CONSEQUENCE: every card's ENTIRE left cast is clipped away, and the LAST card's downward cast is clipped at the grid's bottom edge (the 12px `gap-3` absorbs only the interior ones). The T.W5-R4 cartoon register that `PaletteCard.vue:7-18` is written to celebrate is being amputated by the D.W4 Lane A containment at `PaletteCardGrid.vue:48-52` — a cross-wave contradiction neither wave's own doc records. The pane has 16-24px of gutter (`PalettesPane.vue:27` `px-4 sm:px-6`) so the cast WOULD be visible but for the containment; the grid is the sole clipper.
